newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Storm in Malaysia's Sabah state kills at least 19.
newsitem.headline: Storm in Malaysia's Sabah state kills at least 19.

text.p: At least nineteen people in Malaysia's eastern Sabah state were killed in a storm on Christmas day that caused widespread flooding, the national Bernama news agency said on Thursday.
About 50 houses were washed away when a river overflowed in the interior town of Keningau, Bernama quoted Sabah Police Commissioner Maizan Shaari as saying.
Buildings were damaged elsewhere around the state capital of Kota Kinabalu, and boats off the coast were sunk, Bernama said.
Maizan said four people were killed in Kota Kinabalu, four in the Tuaran area near the capital, and 11 in Keningau.
Sabah Chief Minister Yong Teck Lee on Thursday made an aerial inspection of the damage in Kota Kinabalu and described the storm as one of the worst disasters to hit the state.

The state weather department linked the bad weather conditions to tropical storm Greg, which blew at a speed of more than 50 km (30 miles) an hour from the South China Sea towards Sabah and Sarawak states on the island of Borneo.
